basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'At ille ait: Domine Deus, unde scire possum, quod possessurus sim eam? Non est putandus'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: At ille ait: Domine Deus, unde scire possum, quod possessurus sim eam? Non est putandus Abraham postquam credidit Deo, et reputatum est illi ad justitiam, in fide defecisse, ut diceret: Domine Deus, unde scire possum quod possessurus sim eam? Non enim quasi adhuc incredulus, signum cui credat inquirit, sed obsecrat ut ei rei quam crediderat aliqua similitudo adhiberetur, qua ejus modus agnosceretur; unde significantius vetus habet translatio: Dominator Domine, secundum quid sciam quia haeres ejus ero: sicut non est Virginis Mariae diffidentia cum ait: Quomodo fiet istud, quoniam virum non cognosco (Luc. I, 34)? quod enim futurum erat certa esse, modum quomodo fieret inquirebat. Et hoc cum quaesisset audivit. Denique et hic similitudo est data de animalibus, juvenca, et capra, et ariete, et duabus volucribus, turture et columba, ut secundum haec futurum sciret quod futurum esse non ambigebat.
